- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) and price is trending down, model often over-anticipates reversal; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overreacts with a prolonged upward bias; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: re-estimate mean reversion target based on 5-day sentiment average.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.0–0.5); apply a “sentiment-weighted bias” correction: add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment > 0.2.
- If model forecast is > 2% above recent 7-day high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism; if below 2% below recent 7-day low, increase by 1–2% to avoid underreaction.
